text: Photographers rely on two primary settings within the exposure triangle: aperture and shutter speed. Aperture measures the diameter of the lens opening through which light enters; increasing this size admits more illumination but reduces the depth of field, thereby narrowing the zone that remains sharp. Shutter speed dictates the duration the sensor is exposed to light. Rapid speeds arrest movement in stillness, whereas sluggish speeds produce motion blur. Grasping how these two factors interact is required to generate aesthetically strong photographs.
